description:
## Why this bead exists

Resolves `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate vs external) under ADR-0030's multi-workerd hybrid model. Operator disposition (2026-06-21): **notme can be both — it can be inter-cluster, inter-service, or user-to-service identity, and the mode is a deployment setting.**

This bead carries the implementation of "both topologies, configurable per deployment."

## The three binding modes the operator can pick

Under ADR-0030's multi-workerd substrate with hybrid co-location:

| Mode | Shape | When it fits |
|---|---|---|
| **co-located trusted-tier** | notme runs as a `Bundle.kind.workerd` Worker inside router's workerd process | OSS-launch default. `docker run cloister` = working identity + gateway in one image. Hot-path lease verify is zero-copy. |
| **separate workerd (external)** | notme runs as its own workerd-class process / container (current shape) | Multi-tenant production posture. Independent scaling, independent release cycle, separate IAM. |
| **per-tenant workerd** | notme runs as one of the tenants under ADR-0030's `[[tenants]]` declaration | When a deployment treats notme-the-identity-service AS a tenant of the substrate (rare; emerges for hosted multi-org deployments) |

The substrate must support all three. Operator picks via cluster.toml.

## What ships

1. **notme `bundle build` task** — notme's TS compiled to embeddable JS (`dist/notme-bundle.js`) suitable for cloister's workerd config to `embed`. Sibling bead to file in notme repo.
2. **`cluster.capnp` variant set** — `art-default-bundled` (co-located) + `art-default-split` (external; current) + `art-default-tenant` (per-tenant workerd, future). The schema already reserves `Bundle.kind.workerd`; the variants pick which kind notme uses.
3. **`config.capnp`** gains a second Worker entry conditionally (when bundled variant is selected).
4. **`scripts/emit-compose.mjs` + `scripts/cluster-dev.mjs`** detect the variant and behave correctly (only cloister-router subprocess for bundled, mac-dev launcher elides notme entry).
5. **`docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md`** "Three topologies" section.
6. **ADR amendment** to ADR-0009 (Phase 1) OR fresh ADR — TBD which. The decision routes through `cloister-f289c8`'s supervisor-1 + routing-1 implementation work because the cluster.toml `[[tenants]]` table is the operator surface.

## Operator surface (provisional)

```toml
[[tenants]]
name = "notme-identity"
mode = "co-located"          # | "external" | "per-tenant"
workerd_id = "cloister-router"  # only for co-located; the workerd that hosts the bundle
```

## Coordinated with

- **Parent epic**: `cloister-f289c8` (multi-workerd substrate, vault first)
- **ADR-0030** §D4 (hybrid model)
- **ADR-0013** (slice-grant; co-located trusted-tier still V8-isolate-separated from non-trusted bundles)
- **ADR-0009** Phase 1 (cluster-in-a-pod substrate)
- **Cross-repo**: notme repo needs the bundle-build task before any variant lands

## Acceptance

- Three topology variants expressible in cluster.capnp / cluster.toml
- Operator sets the mode via cluster.toml setting
- All three boot via `task cluster:up`
- `scripts/integration-test.sh` (per `cloister-1b1124`) exercises at least the co-located + external variants
- ADR ratifies the three-topology disposition
- notme-side sibling bead files the bundle-build work

## Status

Open. Filed 2026-06-21 to capture `cloister-db99cd`'s disposition under ADR-0030's hybrid model. Implementation scope is substantial (~half-day to a day for the substrate side; cross-repo coordination for notme bundle build). Blocks on `cloister-f289c8`'s schema-1 (cluster.toml `[[tenants]]` shape) landing first.

description:
ADR-0013 ratified the slice-grant enforcement model: V8 isolate
boundary + service-binding-as-syscall, with cross-bundle isolation
sitting at the binding layer. ADR-0021 went one rung deeper:
per-bundle vault DO instances so SQLite storage is also separated.
The result is **multi-tenancy at the V8-isolate granularity** — N
isolates inside one workerd process, with the substrate refusing
cross-isolate reads through anything other than declared service
bindings.

But the **workerd process itself is shared**. Every tenant on the
same workerd binary inherits:

- The same kernel namespace, the same file-descriptor table, the
  same network namespace, the same `/dev`.
- The same workerd binary version — a workerd-level CVE compromises
  every tenant on that process, not just the bundle that triggered
  it.
- The same V8 build — a V8 sandbox escape that breaks the isolate
  boundary breaks ALL isolates in the process.
- The same process-level resources — file handles, sockets, signal
  handlers.

ADR-0013's slice-grant claim is **load-bearing at the V8 layer and
nowhere else**. The outer ring (workerd process + kernel + V8 binary)
is implicitly trusted by every tenant. For deployments where
tenants are mutually-distrusting peers, that implicit trust is the
gap.

The cred-iso/v2 disposition tracker (`cloister-f289c8`, codified
2026-06-19) gestured at a related-but-narrower direction: Path 4 —
"nono sandbox wraps workerd, kernel-level outer-ring." That path
re-uses one workerd and adds a sandbox AROUND it. This ADR goes
further: **multiple workerd processes**, one per tenant, eliminating
the shared-binary surface entirely.

The trigger to ratify this now is operational, not theoretical: the
substrate's published security claim ("a compromised bundle cannot
read another tenant's vault") is binding only as far as V8's
sandbox holds. Every published V8 0-day moves the goalposts. A
multi-workerd shape lets us define a threat model in which a V8
escape is **not catastrophic** because the blast radius is one
tenant's workerd.

## References

- /dev
- cloister-f289c8

description:
Introduce a **multi-workerd substrate** with four load-bearing
properties:

### D1 — One workerd process per tenant (when isolated)

The substrate gains a deployment shape where each tenant runs in
its own `workerd` process. A compromised V8 isolate cannot reach
another tenant's process address space, file descriptors, or
sockets — process-level isolation provided by the kernel, not by
V8.

This **does not deprecate ADR-0013**. V8 isolate boundaries still
matter inside each per-tenant workerd, for bundles sharing the
same tenant. Slice-grant enforcement is now **two-layered**:

  - **Outer (this ADR):** process-per-tenant. Kernel-enforced.
  - **Inner (ADR-0013):** isolate-per-bundle within a tenant's
    workerd. V8-enforced.

The two compose: a bundle inside tenant T1's workerd cannot read
bundle 2's heap inside T1 (V8 protects), and tenant T1's workerd
cannot read tenant T2's vault DO storage (kernel protects).

### D2 — Polymorphic tenant boundary

The substrate does NOT pre-decide what counts as a tenant. Three
expression modes are first-class, and a deployment may use any one
(or compose them):

| Mode | Boundary | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Per-peer** | One workerd per authenticated signet-identity peer (`subject_fp`) | Strongest isolation; highest process count. Right when peers are mutually-distrusting (e.g. agent constellations across orgs). |
| **Per-bundle** | One workerd per `Bundle.name` in the manifest | Coarser; reuses ADR-0021's per-bundle vault DO seam. Right when bundles ARE the trust boundary and peers within a bundle are trusted. |
| **Per-operator-declared** | A new `[[tenants]]` table in `cluster.toml` declares the boundary explicitly | Operator decides the granularity per deployment. Right for hybrid models — see D4. |

The mechanism (workerd-process-per-tenant) is uniform; the
**definition of tenant** is configurable. Implementation must keep
the three modes expressible from the same substrate primitives.

### D3 — Typed cross-tenant edges (Istio-AppProtocol pattern)

Cross-tenant calls are **first-class**, not deferred. The substrate
does not invent a new network plumbing layer — workerds reach each
other over whatever the deployment provides (loopback HTTP for
single-host pods, UDS for tightly-co-located processes,
CF-tunnel/WARP for off-platform, real network for distributed
deployments). The substrate is intentionally **not** prescribing the
transport.

What the substrate DOES add is a **network-type** label per
cross-tenant edge, modeled on Istio's `AppProtocol` annotation. The
label classifies the traffic semantically — the substrate uses it
for routing, observability, and policy enforcement; the underlying
transport is whatever the operator wires.

Initial label set (extensible; see Open Questions):

```
app_protocol = "http" | "http2" | "grpc" | "tcp" | "tls"
             | "mcp-jsonrpc" | "interlace-capnp" | "capnp-uds"
```

The substrate-specific labels (`mcp-jsonrpc`, `interlace-capnp`,
`capnp-uds`) are first-class: they encode the protocol the substrate
already understands and routes natively. Generic labels (`http`,
`grpc`, etc.) are for tenants that publish non-MCP / non-Interlace
surfaces (`cloister-6fc72e`).

**Explicitly excluded:** raptorq from `ley-line`. raptorq is a
UDP-based reliable transport; the substrate adopts the IDEA of
typed edges but not the specific transport. The substrate stays
transport-agnostic.

### D4 — Vault first, hybrid model preserved

The first concrete migration is the **vault DO**. Rationale:

- Vault is the load-bearing trust boundary in cred-iso/v1
  (ADR-0024). A V8 escape that reaches one tenant's vault reaches
  every other tenant's credentials on the same workerd.
- ADR-0021 already gave each bundle its own DO INSTANCE. The next
  step is each tenant's vault DO living in its own WORKERD PROCESS.
- The vault wire (`/vault/proxy/<service>/<upstream-path>` per
  ADR-0024) is small and well-tested; the migration touches a
  bounded surface.

**Hybrid model.** Some bundles SHOULD remain co-located even in a
multi-workerd world — notably trusted-tier identity (notme), where
co-location with the router gains lease-verification latency that
matters on every authenticated request, and the trust boundary
between notme and router is intentionally shared. The two co-locate
decision beads (`cloister-db99cd` for notme, `cloister-18f456` for
mache) stay open under this ADR — they become questions about
**which tenants share a workerd** rather than "consolidate vs
split." Operator chooses per deployment.

This means the substrate must support:

- `tenant.workerd_id = "<process-name>"` — operator names which
  workerd hosts the tenant.
- Multiple tenants on the same workerd (the hybrid case): they
  share process resources but get separate vault DOs (ADR-0021
  still applies).
- One tenant per workerd (the isolated case): the strict shape this
  ADR adds.

## References

- Bundle.name

- capnp-uds

## Goal

Implements ADR-0030 §A2: SNI + path-prefix dispatch table. Router examines inbound request → resolves tenant via `route_mode` + `route_value` → forwards to that tenant's workerd via service binding (in-process for co-located) or fetcher (for separate workerd).

## Operator surface

```toml
[[tenants]]
name = "alice"
route_mode = "sni"
route_value = "alice.cluster.example.com"

[[tenants]]
name = "bob"
route_mode = "path-prefix"
route_value = "/t/bob/"
```

- New `tenantDispatch` route kind in `manifest/cloister.capnp` (next free ordinal)
- Routing table data structure with O(1) SNI lookup + first-match path-prefix
- Path-prefix mode strips the prefix before forwarding (preserves the inner path the tenant's bundles see)
- Unknown tenant → 404 constant-time (no peer-existence oracle, per threat-model §9 convention)
- Lease verification still happens BEFORE dispatch (the per-tenant scope is part of lease verification)

## Tests required

- **Unit**: routing table lookup (SNI hit/miss; path-prefix longest-match)
- **Integration**: real HTTP request → real tenant workerd dispatch in both modes
- **E2E**: with TLS terminator for SNI mode (mock cert chain)
- **Regression**: single-tenant deployments (no `[[tenants]]` declared) work as before — all requests hit cloister-router's default route table
- **Threat model**: §13 entry — dispatch path doesn't leak tenant existence via timing or response shape

## Refs

- ADR-0030 §A2
- Parent: cloister-0e82d6 (schema-2)
- Threat-model §9 (constant-time 404 pattern)

description:
## Goal

Implements ADR-0030 §A3: three-tier KEK hierarchy.

| Scope | How keyed | Source |
|---|---|---|
| cluster | one root, derived per-tenant via HKDF | ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver picks the root source (Keychain / libsecret / env / file / sign-helper) |
| service | per-service operator-provisioned | declared in `[inputs.*]` or `[[services]]` block, ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver |
| user | per-peer (subject_fp) | DEFERRED to v2 |

## Acceptance

- `vault/src/kek-source.ts` exports `deriveClusterTenantKek(rootKek, tenantName)` using HKDF (Web Crypto subtle.importKey + deriveBits via HKDF, RFC 5869)
- `vault/src/kek-source.ts` exports `loadServiceKek(serviceName, urlSpec)` reading from operator-provisioned URL-spec
- Scope discriminator (`KekScope = {cluster: {tenantName: string}} | {service: {name: string}}`) prevents accidental cross-tier reads
- HKDF info string is canonicalized so the derivation is deterministic across implementations (ref-impl-py extension)
- Threat-model §13 entry: "cluster master compromise = all cluster-tier tenants compromised; service-tier KEKs remain independent"

## Tests required

- **Unit**: HKDF determinism (same input → same output); different tenant_name → independent KEK; cross-tier reads rejected by type
- **Integration**: tenant A's vault DO cannot decrypt tenant B's secret (per-tenant SQLite + per-tenant KEK)
- **E2E**: full vault-proxy roundtrip with multi-tier secrets
- **Regression**: single-tenant deployments (no tenancy declared) use `tenantName = "cluster"` (back-compat)
- **Threat model**: §13 entry on the trust boundary
- **Spec conformance**: cloister-spec/credential-isolation/v1 ref-impl-py extended with three-tier vectors

## Refs

- ADR-0030 §A3
- ADR-0010 (original HKDF framing this resurrects)
- ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver
- ADR-0024 cred-iso/v1
title: f289c8/secrets-three-tier — cluster (HKDF) + service (operator-provisioned) KEK scopes (A3)

description:
## Goal

Extend `docs/security/threat-model.md` §13 (silence-is-evidence) with the new per-tenant-workerd invariants from ADR-0030. The §13 contract is the substrate's published security claim; multi-workerd needs explicit threat-model entries before first deployment.

## What gets added

1. **§13.X — per-tenant disclosure dispatch.** Disclosure endpoint (`/interlace/peers/{fp}`) becomes per-tenant routed. A request to tenant-A's disclosure cannot reveal tenant-B's attestation chain. Constant-time 404 collapses cross-tenant lookups (no peer-existence oracle across tenants).

2. **§13.Y — silence-is-evidence per-tenant.** Tenant T1's workerd terminating does NOT silence T1's attestation ledger, because T1's TrustStore DO lives in T1's workerd. A peer auditing T1's disclosure sees T1's chain regardless of other workerds' state.

3. **§13.Z — cluster master compromise = explicit threat boundary.** Per ADR-0030 §A3, cluster-tier KEKs derive from one root. Compromise of that root = all cluster-tier tenants compromised. This is explicit, not implicit. Service-tier KEKs (operator-provisioned per service) survive cluster-master compromise.

4. **§13.W — workerd-process termination = denial vector.** A compromised tenant cannot terminate sibling tenants' workerds (kernel-enforced); cannot drain sibling tenants' DO storage (per-process boundary). A compromised supervisor IS catastrophic — and is the explicit threat boundary the supervisor choice (ADR-0030 §A1) trades on.

5. **§13.V — cross-tenant edge labels are not authorization.** `app_protocol` labels (ADR-0030 §A4) classify traffic shape; they do NOT grant access. Cross-tenant authorization still flows through Signet leases + per-tenant scopes (ADR-0007).

## Acceptance

- `docs/security/threat-model.md` §13 gains 5 new entries (numbered per existing convention)
- Each entry has the "Attack" / "Mitigation" / "Residual risk" / "Test ref" sub-shape used elsewhere in §13
- Cross-links: ADR-0030 §A1-A5; ADR-0010 (HKDF); ADR-0007 (lease scopes)
- ADR-0030 frontmatter `threat_model` field points at the updated §13
- No code changes; doc-only — but the §13 entries become the contract for the implementation sub-beads' test surfaces (vault-1, router-table, secrets-three-tier all test against this contract)

## Tests required

Doc-only bead — no test code. But the §13 entries ARE the test contract for:
- vault-1's `test/security/cross-tenant-vault.test.ts`
- router-table's "constant-time 404 on unknown tenant" assertion
- secrets-three-tier's "cluster master compromise = all cluster-tier compromised" property
- compose-emitter's "kill one workerd, others survive" integration test

## Refs

- ADR-0030 (the source of the new properties)
- ADR-0007 §11 + threat-model §9 (constant-time 404 pattern this extends)
- ADR-0012 (TrustStore architecture this layers on)
- Parent: cloister-f289c8 epic
title: f289c8/threat-model — §13 extension for per-tenant-workerd disclosure + silence-is-evidence

description: Phase 2 of the ADR-0027/0054 lattice. The matchmaker (cloister-e059ea, PR #179) is a correct algorithm with an EMPTY lattice — no input declares provides/requires. The question is which dimension to declare first, and the answer is egress, not code-intelligence. Grounded in real tenants: lectio reaches api.github.com, api.linear.app, mcp.linear.app, gitlab.com, static.modelcontextprotocol.io; canonical-hours reaches api.github.com, api.linear.app, auth.linear.app, api.openweathermap.org. That is a small, declarable, per-tenant set. Today egress control is PARTIAL: vault-proxy pins upstreamBaseUrl per service (anthropic/openai) which is real enforcement, but the router carries globalOutbound=internet so anything not traversing the proxy is unrestricted, and lint-bundle-isolation Inv 1 only stops CLUSTER-tier bundles acquiring egress at all — there is no per-tenant hostname allowlist anywhere. Proposal: cloister/egress/v1 as the first declared capability — an allowlist of hostnames an input may reach, matched by the matchmaker and enforced at the seams cloister already owns (vault-proxy upstream, globalOutbound wiring, emit-compose network policy), audited via receipts. Why this dimension first: it is a genuine security property (exfiltration boundary), enforceable at existing seams rather than requiring new ones, and tenants genuinely differ on it. Explicitly NOT code-intelligence: llo and mache overlap on ~11 of mache 18 tools, but the operator reports LLO tools are never called and an empty LLO_MCP_URL already disables those backends, so that ambiguity is dead surface. Checked lectio for a reusable allowlist primitive — none exists.
title: Declare cloister/egress/v1 as the first real capability — per-tenant hostname allowlist

description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 during the b89fdb wiring + mermaid lint integration.

## Symptom

`task lint` (which deps `task test`) exits non-zero with:

```
Test Files  37 passed (37)
Tests       569 passed (569)
Errors      2 errors
```

The "Errors" are vitest "Unhandled Rejection" warnings:

```
Error: AttestationIntegrityError: prev_self_ref mismatch ...
Serialized Error: { remote: true }
This error originated in "test/trust-store.test.ts" test file. ...
```

Originating tests:
- `test/trust-store.test.ts > … > RPC propagates AttestationIntegrityError on prev_self_ref mismatch`
- `test/trust-store.test.ts > … > integrity check rejects stale-prev-ref fork without breaking the DO`

Both tests use `await expect(stub.applyAttestation(...)).rejects.toThrow(...)`. The expect matcher catches the rejection (assertion passes), but vitest ALSO tracks the rejection as unhandled because the throw was serialized across the workerd DO RPC boundary (the `{ remote: true }` marker) before the assertion handler caught it. Vitest doesn't recognize the pairing.

## Why this matters

- Pre-existing, ALL tests genuinely pass. The 2 errors are reporter noise, not test failures.
- `task lint` aborts with exit 1, so the inner-loop dev gate is "broken" in a misleading way — agents see red and assume real failures.
- The mermaid-lint that just landed (commit 6a3867a) shares the same gate; same symptom.

## Options

A. **Convert to try/catch**: rewrite the two failing tests to catch + assert on the caught error directly. Drops the rejection out of vitest's tracker. Tested earlier in the session — also showed the warning, so this may not actually solve it.

B. **Vitest config: `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors`**: workers-pool option that suppresses the warning. Loses signal for real future regressions.

C. **Wrap RPC errors in a Result-shape**: change `TrustStore.applyAttestation` to return `{ ok: false, error: "..." }` instead of throwing. Caller still gets the rejection-like semantics; vitest sees a normal value cross the boundary, not a rejection. Cleanest but most invasive.

D. **Catch on the server side, re-throw with `data` payload via JsonRpcInvocationError-like wrapper**: encode the integrity-failure as a controlled rejection with a custom name. Vitest may pair it correctly.

Recommend C (Result-shape return). The integrity error is a defense-in-depth check that should NEVER fire in production; treating it as a Result instead of an exception is more honest.

## Files

- `src/trust-store.ts` (applyAttestation RPC method)
- `src/storage/peer-attestations.ts` (helper signature)
- `test/trust-store.test.ts` (assertion-style update)
- `test/storage/peer-attestations.test.ts` (assertion-style update)

## Acceptance

- `task test` exits 0 cleanly (no "Errors: 2")
- `task lint` exits 0 cleanly
- All existing assertions still hold
- Integrity-failure path is still tested + observable

## Refs

- bdcbe7 — where these tests landed
- mermaid lint commit 6a3867a — the new gate now affected
title: vitest "unhandled rejection" warnings on AttestationIntegrityError tests

comments.text:
**2026-05-10 gating answer**: mache compute is **Go** (world 3 from the bead's framing). With one important clarification:

> "mache is in go. But LLO is how it gets TS / LSP data."

So mache doesn't directly do tree-sitter / language-server work — it **delegates to ley-line-open**. Mache is more accurately framed as a code-intelligence orchestrator that consumes LLO's TS/LSP output. That changes the porting cost:

- **Full port** = mache's Go orchestration logic → wasm or TS, PLUS LLO's separate Rust+TS stack would need to be reachable from inside cloister's workerd via service binding. That's substantial — both repos need work.
- **Stub port** = a thin TS wrapper inside cloister-router that proxies `mache_*` MCP tools over to a sibling LLO bundle. Effectively keeps mache as an "MCP front-end" reachable from inside workerd via service binding, with the actual compute still happening in LLO over UDS. But that just moves the cross-process hop from cloister-router→mache to cloister-router→llo — no real co-location benefit.

**Net**: mache as a workerd-bundle isn't a clean win because the compute it dispatches lives in LLO anyway. The substrate-isolation value (`cloister-ac30e7`'s first workerd-bundle Worker) needs a real TOOL bundle that EXECUTES inside workerd, not just an orchestration shim.

**Defer until / unless a real workerd-bundle Worker shows up.** The likely first one isn't mache — it's a hypothetical "small custom MCP tool a user writes in TS and ships as a bundle." That's the use case the substrate-isolation model in ADR-0013 was designed for, and it's also what would actually exercise `cloister-ac30e7`'s lint.

**Holding open with a "defer past 1.0" note.** Not closing — it's a real future decision, just not one to force a verdict on today.

comments.author: rsry-mcp
comments.text:
**Gating question answered 2026-06-21: mache is World 3 (Go-native).** Combined with ADR-0030 the bead is closeable.

## Mache compute inventory

Direct read of `~/remotes/art/mache`:

| Signal | Reading |
|---|---|
| Source language | 336 .go files; **0 .ts source files** (407 .py + 124 .rs are test fixtures only) |
| `go.mod` | `module github.com/agentic-research/mache`, `go 1.26` |
| Tree-sitter binding | `github.com/smacker/go-tree-sitter` (Go bindings) + **cgo edge at `internal/treesitter/elixir/binding.go`** |
| SQLite | `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure-Go transpile — OK) |
| Other Go-native deps | `fsnotify`, `go-billy`, `go-nfs`, `BurntSushi/toml`, `hcl/v2`, `mcp-go`, `roaring`, `ojg`, `zeebo/blake3` |

cgo through tree-sitter parsers is the killer. World-3 per the bead's own taxonomy: "Real port required. Either rewrite compute in TS or do a substantial wasm porting effort. Likely > 1 week. Multi-session."

## ADR-0030 reframes this further

The bead's original framing was "co-locate into cloister-router's workerd as a `Bundle.kind.workerd` V8-isolate Worker." ADR-0030 (commit 52fbf91, 2026-06-21) ratifies a different direction: **multi-workerd-process-per-tenant**. Under that direction:

- "Co-locate mache as workerd-bundle in router's process" — **NOT the right shape under ADR-0030**, regardless of compute language
- "mache runs as its own workerd-class process in the cluster" — **already the shape today** (external bundle, `mache:0.8.0` image, UDS to router)

So whether mache is world-1, 2, or 3, the **deployment-shape question this bead poses is moot under ADR-0030's hybrid model**: mache stays as its own process (which it is today), and the question "should it consolidate into router's workerd" becomes "no, we're going the opposite direction — more process boundaries, not fewer."

## Disposition

**Closing as wontfix-per-ADR-0030.** Two independent reasons converge:

1. Compute world-3 means the original consolidation path requires a multi-week port.
2. ADR-0030 inverts the direction entirely — we want more workerd processes, not fewer, and mache-as-external-process is the right shape under that direction.

If a future world-1/world-2 port of mache happens (e.g. a TS rewrite of the compute layer), a NEW bead under the multi-workerd epic (`cloister-f289c8`) would file the mache-as-tenant-workerd work; this bead's framing is too coupled to the consolidate-into-router-workerd direction to be useful.

cloister-ac30e7 (substrate-property lint) still waits for first `Bundle.kind.workerd` Worker — that will come from `cloister-f289c8`'s vault-1 sub-bead, not this bead's reuse-mache-as-workerd-bundle path.

Closing.

description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from a session-end design question. Sibling to `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate); same shape, different bundle.

## Question

mache uses SQLite as its persistence layer — **workerd-compliant by construction**, since DO storage IS SQLite (`ctx.storage.sql`). mache also no longer uses FUSE (correction from earlier session framing — see commit history). Both facts open a door that didn't exist when `cluster.capnp` was first written.

`cluster.capnp` today declares mache as an `external` bundle (subprocess container, image `mache:0.8.0`, reached over UDS). `Bundle.kind.workerd` is schema-reserved for co-located V8 isolates inside cloister-router's workerd. **Mache could move from external to workerd-bundle** if its compute layer ports to TS/wasm.

This bead is the decision point.

## Gating question

**Where does mache's compute live today, and can it run inside workerd?**

Three worlds, three different answers:

| Mache's compute is... | Path to workerd-bundle | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| TS / JS already | Direct. Add Bundle.kind.workerd entry, wire bindings, embed dist. | Half-day |
| Wasm-compiled (or compilable) — tree-sitter wasm, embedding models wasm | Indirect but straightforward. Workerd loads wasm; JS shim exposes the API surface. | Day or two depending on cgo edges |
| Still Go-native (cgo for tree-sitter, native embedding deps) | Real port required. Either rewrite compute in TS or do a substantial wasm porting effort. Likely > 1 week. | Multi-session |

If mache is in worlds 1 or 2, this is a small, high-leverage move. If world 3, it's a real decision about whether to port.

## Why move it (co-locate as workerd-bundle)

1. **OSS-launch ergonomics**: combined with `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate), the deploy story becomes "docker run cloister-bundled" — gateway + identity + code intel in ONE image. Bead state (rosary, Go + dolt) stays as a sidecar. Reducing 4 containers → 2 is a massive operator-experience win for the simple-deploy story.
2. **In-process service binding**: mache calls become zero-copy IPC. No UDS round-trip, no capnp serialization for the wire. Latency benefit similar to the lease batching from `cloister-ee51b8` — workerd cross-process even via UDS is ~hundreds of µs; in-process service binding is essentially free.
3. **First real workerd-bundle Worker unblocks `cloister-ac30e7`**: the substrate-property lint (no globalOutbound, no secret bindings) has been blocked-on-first-real-user since being filed. Mache as a tool-bundle satisfies that. Combined with notme (workerd-bundle but trusted-tier), there'd be both tiers of bundle Worker exercising the schema.
4. **Matches the substrate model**: ADR-0013 ratified that bundles reach vault/notme via service bindings. mache's bundle-level identity becomes meaningful — it'd be a tool-bundle Worker (cluster-tier) consuming the substrate's services.

## Why NOT move it (keep external)

1. **Compute-layer gating** (the big one). If mache is Go-today and the port is multi-week, the cost likely exceeds the operator-experience win for OSS launch. Defer to a 1.1 or 2.0 milestone.
2. **Independent release cycle**: mache versions independently of cloister; co-location forces version-lockstep or a bundle-pinning build step.
3. **Local-vs-prod divergence** (same as `cloister-db99cd` notme case): on CF Workers prod, mache as a Worker would be a separate Worker deployment regardless. The single-process win only holds in workerd-local; CF will cross workers either way.
4. **Image size**: cloister-bundled gets bigger if it embeds mache's wasm/JS.

## What this does NOT change

Same as `cloister-db99cd`: the security model. V8 isolates separate heaps regardless of single-vs-multi-process. Mache's heap is unreachable from cloister-router's whether they share a workerd binary or run in different containers.

## What ships if "co-locate"

Depends on which compute-layer world mache is in. If world 1 (TS already) or world 2 (wasm-compilable):

1. **mache** ships a "bundle build" — its compute compiled to a single embeddable JS file (`dist/mache-bundle.js`) suitable for cloister's `config.capnp` to `embed`. New task in mache's Taskfile.
2. **cloister/config.capnp** adds a third Worker entry (mache bundle Worker), service binding declarations.
3. **cluster.capnp** gets a variant where mache is `kind = (workerd = ...)` instead of `external`. Original `external` variant stays for operators who want separate processes.
4. **`scripts/emit-compose.mjs`** + **`scripts/cluster-dev.mjs`** detect the variant and elide the mache subprocess for the bundled variant.
5. **docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md** "Three topologies" section (1+2+3 of: bundled, sidecar, k8s-pod).
6. **ADR amendment** to ADR-0009 (Phase 1) noting the topology choices, OR a new ADR that ratifies "bundled-by-default for OSS launch."

If world 3 (port needed): file a separate "mache compute port to wasm or TS" bead in mache; this bead waits on that.

## Cross-repo coordination

Requires changes in mache — the bundle build. **File a sibling bead in mache once the gating question is answered** (which world mache is in). The mache-side bead is small if it's world 1/2; substantial if world 3.

## Sibling beads + cross-refs

- **`cloister-db99cd`** — notme co-locate decision. Same shape. Both could land together for the "docker run cloister-bundled" story.
- **`cloister-ac30e7`** — substrate-property lint, blocked on first workerd-bundle Worker. This bead unblocks it.
- **`cloister-be0607`** — cluster-in-a-pod substrate that makes this possible.
- **`mache-172a50`** — mache's in-repo apko/melange (the external-container path). Stays valuable EITHER way; co-location doesn't kill the separate-container deploy option, it adds a new shape alongside.
- **ADR-0013** — slice-grant enforcement (orthogonal; mache co-located doesn't change the security model).
- **notme/docs/design/009-identity-gated-runtime.md** — the "co-located Workers in one process" pattern that informs both this and db99cd.

## Acceptance

- The gating question is answered: which compute-layer world is mache in?

description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Integration gate for the 4 image beads dispatched today.

## What needs to happen

Once the four upstream image beads land, we need to verify each image **boots in isolation** AND that they **compose correctly** via cloister's `cluster.capnp` topology. Two failure modes we're guarding against:

1. **Individual breakage**: an image builds but doesn't actually serve its wire (e.g. mache image runs but the capnp-over-UDS handshake doesn't match what cloister-router speaks).
2. **Compose-time breakage**: each image works alone but the multi-bundle wiring fails (UDS perms wrong, port conflict, service-binding name mismatch, init-order race).

## Validation matrix

### A — Separately (each image, standalone smoke)

For each of `notme:0.1.0`, `rosary:0.2.0`, `mache:0.8.0`, `ley-line-open:0.1.0`:
- `docker load` + `docker run` with the args from `cluster.capnp` (or the equivalent for llo, which isn't in cluster.capnp yet — use llo's own MCP entrypoint).
- Verify the wire responds:
  - **notme**: HTTP 200 on `/health` (port 8788)
  - **rosary**: capnp ToolCall `tools/list` over UDS at the mounted socket → non-empty response
  - **mache**: capnp ToolCall `tools/list` over UDS → mache's tool surface
  - **llo**: HTTP/MCP request on its declared port → tool surface
- Container exits cleanly on SIGTERM (no orphaned children, socket cleaned up).

### B — Together (cluster compose)

Run `task cluster:up` (or whatever the compose entrypoint becomes). Verify:
- All four bundles start (init order: cloister-router last, after sibling UDS sockets exist).
- cloister-router can reach mache + rosary + notme via service bindings.
- llo is reachable from cloister-router (today: HTTP via LLO_MCP_URL; eventually capnp-over-UDS once it joins the bundle list).
- End-to-end: a request through cloister-router that needs ALL four succeeds.
- `task cluster:down` cleans up — no orphaned containers, no leftover UDS sockets.

## Acceptance

- Test script (`scripts/integration-test.sh` or Taskfile target `task cluster:test`) runs A then B.
- CI-friendly (exit codes, no interactive prompts).
- Documented failure modes for each rung — operators running this need to know where to look.

## Dependencies

Blocked on:
- notme-1699ec (notme image)
- rosary-16df06 (rosary image)
- mache-172a50 (mache image)
- ley-line-open-17739e (llo image)

## Out of scope

- Co-location decisions (cloister-db99cd, cloister-18f456) — those change the matrix shape but don't block this work.
- Cluster.capnp adding llo as a bundle — separate follow-up.
- Performance / load testing.

description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 by the surface-3 bench in `cloister-e4daae`. **Original misfiled as `rosary-1a0362` — refiling here in cloister, which owns the disclosure endpoint code.**

## Finding

The disclosure endpoint (`GET /interlace/peers/{fp}`) advertises a constant-time 404 across error cases (§9.4 + §9.2 of the threat model). The implementation IS byte-identical at the response body level (same `content-length`, same body), but **timing diverges by ~17× between cases**:

| Case | Mean | Code path |
|---|---:|---|
| Peer doesn't exist (no-peer 404) | ~0.53 ms | TWO DO RPCs: `listAttestationsForPeer` + `listPendingForPeer` |
| Cursor tampered (bad-cursor 404) | ~0.03 ms | Early return; DO never touched |
| Auth fail (lease invalid 404) | (unmeasured this session) | Likely early-return like bad-cursor |

A colocated attacker timing requests at sub-ms resolution can distinguish:
- "this peer doesn't exist" (DO round-trip taken)
- "your cursor was tampered" / "your lease was bad" (early-return)

On a real WAN, RTT variance probably swamps the 0.5 ms delta. **In-DC, this is a real oracle.** Cloister's threat model claims §9.4 — the implementation didn't measure it. Bench at `test/perf/disclosure-endpoint.test.ts` shows the exact distribution.

## Fix options

**Option A — slow-equalize (recommended)**: every 404 path always performs the two DO RPCs, then discards the result if the cursor / auth was bad. Cost: every bad-cursor request pays ~0.5 ms it didn't have to. Benefit: the §9.4 invariant becomes load-bearing in code, not just claimed.

**Option B — never call the DO for any 404**: the no-peer case would have to be sniffed from somewhere cheaper (a peer-existence cache?). Saves cost but adds a cache layer + a different timing surface (cache hit vs miss). Probably worse than Option A.

**Option C — match-the-fast-path**: rewrite the no-peer 404 to early-return WITHOUT consulting the DO, by treating "no rows" as indistinguishable from "no peer." Requires reworking how the disclosure endpoint detects peer existence; might leak a different oracle.

**Recommendation: Option A.** Same code shape as the cert-chain verifier (which always does the full work to avoid early-return oracles). Add a regression test that times both paths and asserts they're within X µs of each other.

## Threat model update needed

`docs/security/threat-model.md` §9.4 currently asserts constant-time. **Either**:
- Land the fix + add a test that pins the invariant empirically (the test should fail if the timing delta exceeds some threshold), OR
- Downgrade §9.4 to "byte-identical response, NOT timing-identical — in-DC adversaries have a sub-ms oracle." This is the honest disposition until Option A lands.

## Acceptance

- Option A implemented in `src/routes/disclosure.ts`: all 404 paths perform equivalent work before returning.
- Regression test in `test/routes/disclosure.test.ts` that asserts the timing delta between no-peer and bad-cursor 404 is below some threshold (50µs? — pick based on what the bench can stably measure).
- `task lint` stays green.
- `task bench:disclosure` re-run shows the two paths' means within ~10% of each other.
- Threat model §9.4 updated to point at the test + the bench doc as the load-bearing assertion.

## Refs

- `docs/perf/2026-05-10-disclosure-endpoint.md` — bench finding
- `cloister-e4daae` — parent perf bead this came out of
- `cloister-c7a184` — original "constant-time error path" bead (closed; only addressed the body shape, not timing)
- ADR-0007 §13.2 — the §9.4 invariant chains into the disclosure security claim
- `rosary-1a0362` — original misfiled location; close as moved-to-cloister
title: Disclosure endpoint 404 is NOT constant-time — §9.4 invariant violated (timing oracle)

description:
## Discovery

While shipping cloister-cedcf3 Phase 1 (perTenant field), I added the field to `manifest/cluster.capnp` and regen'd `src/generated/cluster.zod.ts`. The zod schema correctly required `perTenant: boolean`. But `src/manifest/cluster-types.ts` ALSO declares a Bundle interface (hand-maintained) and was NOT updated. This created a runtime/type mismatch: `cluster.zod.ts` Bundle required perTenant; `cluster-types.ts` Bundle did not.

## Why it matters

Today's chain has TWO Bundle types:

1. `src/generated/cluster.zod.ts` — generated from `manifest/cluster.capnp` via schema-bridge. Always in sync with the capnp schema.
2. `src/manifest/cluster-types.ts` — hand-maintained TS interface. Drifts every time the capnp schema changes.

When the two disagree, tsc throws at the boundary (e.g. cluster.ts assigned to Bundle interface). I caught this fire's drift via tsc but the path was indirect — the immediate error was "perTenant doesn't exist in type 'Bundle'" pointing at cluster.ts, not at the missing field in cluster-types.ts.

## Recommended fix

Make `cluster-types.ts` re-export Bundle from `cluster.zod.ts` so there's only one source of truth. The hand-maintained file probably has docstrings + utility types that are valuable — keep those but stop duplicating Bundle/Wire/etc. interfaces that schema-bridge generates.

Sketch:
```ts
// src/manifest/cluster-types.ts
export type { Bundle, Wire, StoragePolicy } from "../generated/cluster.zod.js";
// Keep: discriminated-union helpers, type guards, ad-hoc utility types
// the substrate uses but capnp doesn't model.
```

## Scope

1. Audit `src/manifest/cluster-types.ts` — list which interfaces duplicate what's in `cluster.zod.ts`
2. Re-export from cluster.zod.ts; remove hand-authored duplicates
3. Verify no consumers depend on shape differences (e.g. optional fields)
4. Update imports across src/ + scripts/ + tests/

## Why P3

The runtime symptom is "tsc errors after schema change" — annoying but not silently incorrect. The duplicate types DON'T cause production bugs; they cause developer friction.

## Related

- `cloister-cedcf3` Phase 1 (the drift that surfaced this)
- ADR-0025 (the bidi pipeline that should make types single-source)
title: Consolidate duplicate Bundle type — cluster-types.ts (hand-maintained) + cluster.zod.ts (generated) duplicate the same interface

description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 closing cloister-b89fdb. The test fixture cert (`gen-fixture.rs`) has hard-coded validity `not_before = 1700000000, not_after = 1700000300` (Nov 14, 2023). Wall-clock has passed it by ~2.5 years.

## Today's coverage

Two test suites work around this:
- `test/lease-middleware.test.ts` — passes `nowMs` as an explicit arg, pins time-in-cert-window manually
- `test/mcp-auth.test.ts` — bypasses SELF.fetch entirely, uses direct McpEdgeRoute.handle(req, env) so wall-clock isn't involved

What's NOT covered: an end-to-end SELF.fetch happy-path test that actually mints + signs + dispatches against the real Worker. The clock-skew check would catch it.

## Options when this starts mattering

1. **Mint fixtures at test-setup time** — Run `gen-fixture` with `not_before = now() - 60s, not_after = now() + 600s` before each test session. Heavy: requires Rust + wasm rebuild in the test path.

2. **CLOCK_OVERRIDE env binding for tests** — workerd reads it instead of `Date.now()`. Smells like a bypass; ADR-0007's spirit pushes back.

3. **Use vitest fake timers + worker test mode** — workerd-test compat unclear. Worth a 30-min spike.

4. **Sliding-window fixtures** — gen-fixture takes a `--validity-from-now` flag; checked into repo as `cert-chain-current.ts` regenerated by a CI step. Tradeoff: fixture commits are noisy in git, but they're deterministic per minute.

## When this matters

Today: it doesn't — both suites cover the auth surface adequately. The unwritten test is "full happy path via SELF.fetch with auth gate on." If we ever need that (e.g. for a smoke test that exercises a real Worker boot + the entire wire), this bead's substrate needs to land.

Priority: **3** (low). Park until someone trips over it.

## Refs

- cloister-b89fdb — mcp.ts wire arc that surfaced this
- `test/wire/fixtures/cert-chain.ts` — the fixture
- `rs/crates/sign/examples/gen-fixture.rs` — fixture minter

acceptance_criteria: A digest on the build-cache/v1 wire is self-describing: either the prefix names the algorithm actually used, or the format carries an explicit algorithm field. A consumer that trusts the label without BlobStore.put dual-verification cannot select the wrong algorithm. Regression test asserts a mislabeled digest is rejected rather than silently dual-verified.

comments.author: rsry-cli
comments.text:
EGRESS FINDING — the mislabel is re-emitted outward, not merely accepted inward. Materially changes the containment story recorded when this bead was filed.

Audited every sha256: occurrence in src/ (excluding generated). Two honest categories: bundle-token-verify.ts deriveSubjectFp genuinely calls crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256") and labels it sha256: (truncated to 12 bytes — a fingerprint namespace, correctly separate from 64-hex content digests), and various manifest/ doc comments describing the form. No second dishonest CONSTRUCTOR exists, so the algorithm lie is isolated to the build-cache/v1 path — good news.

The bad news is where that path leads. oci-registry.ts:698-705:
    storageKey = verified.key;                 // may be BLAKE3 hex
    const storageRef = `sha256:${storageKey}`; // relabelled sha256:
and manifestResponse / manifestHeadResponse (lines ~821, 824, 834):
    "docker-content-digest": `sha256:${digest}`
    "etag":                  `"sha256:${digest}"`

So content pushed under the build-cache/v1 convention is served back over standard OCI paths with a sha256: label over BLAKE3 bytes, in docker-content-digest AND ETag, to arbitrary clients.

Why this matters more than the ingress case: the containment argument on this bead was "nothing recomputes the digest — it is used as an address." That holds INSIDE cloister. It does not hold for external clients, who are entitled to verify docker-content-digest and whose tooling commonly does. Such a client computes SHA-256 over the body, gets a mismatch, and concludes CONTENT CORRUPTION — the failure is attributed to the wrong cause entirely, and the remediation it suggests (re-pull, distrust the registry) is unrelated to the actual defect.

That also means the safety is thinner than "one call site dual-verifies": the dual-verify protects the WRITE, while the read path re-asserts an algorithm nothing verified on the way out.

Not fixed here — recorded because it changes how the fix should be scoped. A correct fix has to address egress labelling, not only ingress acceptance, and the OCI-client-capability constraint in ADR-0056 (keep sha256: on /v2/ because real clients expect it) is in direct tension with it: we cannot honestly label BLAKE3 content on a surface whose clients only understand sha256. That tension is the actual design problem, and it argues that build-cache/v1 content may simply not belong on the standard OCI read path under a sha256: label at all.

Verified by reading, not inferred: grep of all sha256: sites, plus lines 698-705 and 813-836 read directly.

description:
CLAUDE.md:186 — "The build-cache/v1 wire overloads the OCI `sha256:` prefix with BLAKE3 hex — `BlobStore.put` dual-verifies against both algorithms." docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:367 says the same; the encoding rule lives in leyline-schema-spec/build-cache/v1/wire/digest-encoding.md.

The label asserts an algorithm the bytes do not use. This is an ACTIVE MISSTATEMENT, not an omission: a third party re-deriving the digest under the declared scheme computes the wrong value and concludes tampering, while an attacker or a bug that swaps algorithms produces something that still looks well-formed.

Why it is contained today, and why that containment is thin: it survives only because BlobStore.put happens to dual-verify against both algorithms. That is a property of ONE CALL SITE, not of the format. Any other consumer that trusts the prefix — a new backend, an external auditor, a future verifier — selects the wrong algorithm with no signal. The safety is incidental rather than structural.

Why this matters more than it looks: cloister trust surface is built on the claim that a third party can verify attestations independently (threat-model 404 / D.4, closed by cloister-bdef0c: the disclosure response carries master_public_key precisely so an auditor needs nothing external). A digest whose label lies is the one thing that cannot be independently verified, because the verifier cannot know what to recompute. The scheme label must be BOUND to the bytes, not adjacent to them — otherwise the label can be changed without perturbing the digest and the artifact still appears valid.

Cross-repo context (LLO analysis, 2026-07-27): this is the third independent sighting of one substrate gap. LLO has SHA-256 hashing in production sheaf/src inside a BLAKE3-locked substrate (ley-line-open-b61cd6); rosary has a JSONL export whose byte order is not canonical so its own hash is unstable (rosary-afdc19). Those two are ABSENCES — a missing declaration, a missing sort. Cloister is the active misstatement and is the worst of the three. Three unrelated layers reaching the same failure is what makes this a substrate gap rather than local sloppiness.

Prior art for the fix: LLO leyline-core::partition implements a tagged fold keyed via BLAKE3 new_derive_key with every variable-length field length-prefixed, so the address commits to the decomposition rather than the concatenation. Per ADR-0035 cloister should BRIDGE that primitive (as src/wire/cas-hash.ts already bridges leyline-cas-ffi) rather than reimplement it.

Filed independently of the tool-call event-plane design thread that surfaced it, per LLO recommendation — this is a latent trap in shipped code and should not wait on that decade.
title: build-cache/v1 digest prefix asserts sha256: while carrying BLAKE3 bytes

comments.text:
Landed in commit 538ba30 on main.

## What's in
- Fault-injection seam extended to BlobStore.put (`blobStorePut` key) and BeadStore.create (`beadStoreWrite` key). Same globalThis.__cloisterTestFaults Map as fff647; production-inert; keyed by hop name.
- Two new test cases in test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts:
  - fault-at-BlobStore.put (~95 LoC): no downstream writes; idempotent CAS yields same digest on retry.
  - fault-at-BeadStore.write (~95 LoC): BlobStore digest landed before fault; no bead row; no TrustStore write (short-circuit invariant verified); retry produces same digest, bead row, attestation.
- threat-model §13.4 replaced "acknowledged" framing with explicit coverage table + invariant: "every cross-DO state-mutating hop is fault-injection-tested. New cross-DO sequences MUST add a corresponding test case before landing."
- AGENTS.md pre-PR guidance gained a one-liner pointing at §13.4.

## Findings to flag
1. **Throw across workerd RPC = vitest unhandled-rejection noise (revisited).** First implementation had BlobStore.put throw on fault; vitest test pool reports that as a test failure even when the orchestrator catches cleanly (same root cause as fff647's switch to Result returns). Fix: BlobStore.put returns a sentinel `BLOB_PUT_FAULT_DIGEST` (exported, not a valid hex digest, fails-closed downstream). BeadStore.create throws — but its in-DO dispatch() try/catch converts to a JSON-RPC error response, so the throw never crosses the RPC boundary. Both paths work; pattern documented in seam headers.
2. **Orchestrator short-circuit was NOT automatic.** The fff647 orchestrator (`runBeadCreatePipeline`) blindly called BeadStore step 2 even when step 1 failed, and step 3 even when step 2's JSON-RPC returned an error. Test orchestrator was extended to check failure per-hop and bail. This is the right behavior to assert because **there is no production orchestrator yet** — the test orchestrator IS the spec for what production will do when wired (per the file's own comment ~line 108). When production wires this in, it must short-circuit the same way; the BeadStore-fault test will catch a regression where TrustStore.applyAttestation runs anyway.
3. **No orchestrator bugs found in src/.** The cross-DO sequence lives only in the test orchestrator today. `src/beads.ts` has zero cross-DO awareness (it's intra-DO per §13.4); no leakage past short-circuit there to fix. The pipeline is still test-only TypeScript.

## Counts
- baseline: 636 tests / 43 files
- post: 638 tests / 43 files (task lint exits 0 clean)

## Out of scope (not done)
- Did not build the generic property-test framework (Option A). One pipeline, three hops; manual enumeration was lower friction.
- Did not wire the orchestrator into src/. That's the "follow-up bead" referenced in the test file header (line ~107-108).
- Did not push.

Leaving open for human review.

description:
Filed 2026-05-10 as a follow-up to the threat-model §13.4 audit + the user's call that "this is solvable, write it."

## What this closes

Threat-model §13.4 audited every cross-DO state-mutating sequence in the codebase. **One was found and closed (lease pipeline via `cloister-ee51b8`).** The audit also documented that **the recovery paths are tested at the HELPER level (`pending_attestations.test.ts`) and at ONE e2e level (`cross-do-recovery.test.ts` via `cloister-fff647`) but NOT as a substrate-wide property.**

The remaining risk: a future contributor adds a new cross-DO write sequence, forgets to test recovery at every failure point, and the §13.4 invariant becomes "audited at a moment in time" instead of "structurally maintained." This bead closes that gap by generalizing the fff647 fault-injection pattern to a property test that scales as the inventory grows.

## Concrete scope

### Inventory (from §13.4 — adjust as new sequences land)

| Sequence | Hops | Failure surfaces |
|---|---|---|
| `bead_create` flow | BlobStore.put → BeadStore.write → TrustStore.applyAttestation | After step 1, after step 2, after step 3 |
| Vault credential write | (intra-DO today) | n/a |
| Future cross-DO writes | TBD | enforce via this bead's test pattern |

### Two design options (pick at scoping)

**Option A — a generic property-test framework**
- Extend `globalThis.__cloisterTestFaults` (the fff647 fault seam) to support fault-injection at every cross-DO RPC method, keyed by method-name.
- A `test/security/cross-do-fault-injection.test.ts` enumerates the §13.4 inventory, for each (sequence, fail-at-step-k) tuple it sets the fault, runs the sequence, asserts:
  - State before the failure is consistent (idempotent put OR rolled back)
  - Retry path (where defined) restores consistency
  - No partial state visible externally as §13.2 misbehavior
- Adding a new cross-DO sequence means adding one entry to the inventory list; the property-test runner handles the rest.
- **Cost**: a real framework (~200-300 LoC). Maintenance burden if the fault seam needs to grow.

**Option B — one test file per cross-DO sequence**
- Today: `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts` (the fff647 file) covers bead_create with fault-at-TrustStore-step.
- This bead: extend that file (or split it) to cover fault-at-BlobStore-step + fault-at-BeadStore-step for the bead_create sequence. Same pattern, more cases.
- Future cross-DO writes: a new test file with the same pattern, manually-enumerated cases.
- **Cost**: less framework, more boilerplate per sequence. But each test is explicit + easy to read.

**Recommendation: Option B.** The framework cost (Option A) only pays off if cloister grows several new cross-DO sequences fast — and the design intent (per ADR-0012) is that cross-DO writes use idempotent BlobStore puts so the recovery story is uniform. Manual enumeration scales fine to 3-5 sequences; if it ever grows past that, switch to A.

## Acceptance (Option B path)

1. **Extend `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts`** with two new test cases for the bead_create sequence:
   - **fault-at-BlobStore-step**: inject BlobStore.put failure. Assert: no bead row in BeadStore, no attestation in TrustStore, no pending row. Clear fault, retry the bead_create call — assert full success (idempotent BlobStore put returns the same digest, downstream writes proceed).
   - **fault-at-BeadStore-step**: BlobStore.put succeeded (digest exists in BlobStore), then BeadStore.write fails. Assert: digest in BlobStore (idempotent, reusable), no bead row in BeadStore, no attestation in TrustStore. Clear fault, retry — assert success without duplicating the BlobStore digest.

2. **Extend the fault seam** (`globalThis.__cloisterTestFaults`) to support `"blobStorePut"` and `"beadStoreWrite"` keys alongside the existing `"applyAttestation"`. Same inert-in-production contract (Map check at the top of the method; production code sees `undefined`).

3. **Document the invariant in threat-model §13.4**: replace the "test-coverage gap (acknowledged, not closed)" paragraph (if any remnant) with a sentence noting: "Every hop in every cross-DO sequence in the inventory above is fault-injection-tested at `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts`. New cross-DO sequences MUST add a corresponding test case before landing."

4. **Update `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`** (whichever holds the "before-PR checklist" type guidance) with a one-liner: "Any new cross-DO state-mutating sequence requires a fault-injection test per the §13.4 audit pattern."

## What "fault-injection" means concretely

Per fff647: a test-mode-only Map check at the top of each cross-DO RPC method. Production code path is one extra `Map.has()` call (constant cost) and unreachable from outside test context. No new env vars, no DO methods that exist only for tests. The `globalThis.__cloisterTestFaults` Map is set/cleared by the test; production reads `undefined` and short-circuits.

## What NOT to do

- **No production-reachable fault-injection backdoor.** If you can't get to a clearly-test-only shape, file a sub-bead and stop; don't ship a half-safe shim.
- **Don't add fault injection to the LEASE PIPELINE** — that's now atomic (one transactionSync per ee51b8), no cross-DO recovery to test. Stay scoped to bead_create.
- **Don't generalize ahead of need.** Option A's framework is tempting; Option B is cheaper today. Pick A only if the inventory grows beyond 3-5 sequences.
- **Don't push.** Local commit only.

## Pre-flight

`task lint` should be at 636 tests (post-1c42ae). Wasm artifact required for some adjacent tests; run `task rs:sign:wasm` if missing.

## Commit

Set `.rsry-bead-id` to this bead's ID (you'll see it once filed). Prefix `[cloister-XXX]`. Don't close — comment with results.

## Refs

- `cloister-fff647` — the one e2e fault-injection test we already have (TrustStore failure point for bead_create); this bead generalizes it across the other steps + future sequences.
- `cloister-ee51b8` — closed the lease-pipeline atomicity gap (one-transaction RPC); reduces the cross-DO surface this bead covers.
- ADR-0012 — content-addressed handoff design (the recovery model this property test exercises).
- threat-model §13.4 — the audit table this bead's tests pin.
- threat-model §8 — "the dangerous case" framing (3 succeeds, 4 fails); this bead generalizes the recovery story.
title: Substrate-wide cross-DO fault-injection property test (generalize fff647 to the §13.4 inventory)

The old row conflated two distinct surfaces.

description:
Filed 2026-05-10 as a follow-up to `cloister-e61909` (Python ref impl, closed). All 27 conformance cases passed but the agent flagged three documentation inconsistencies the test vectors resolved unambiguously. Future implementors shouldn't have to dig.

## What needs to change

### 1. Claims JSON key ordering

- **`interlace-spec/0.1.0/README.md` §1** says "alphabetical keys"
- **§2.1 + the test vectors + cloister's Rust gen-fixture + cloister's TS impl + the Python ref impl** all use *declaration order*: `epk, nb, na, ep, pf, sc`
- Reconcile: §1 is wrong. Fix the wording to say "declaration order as listed in §2.1" (or move §2.1's table up to §1 for clarity).

### 2. `cert_fp` definition

- **README §3 bullet** says `cert_fp = sha256(canonical_claims_json)`
- **§4.1 + all three implementations** (Rust, TS, Python) say `cert_fp = sha256_hex(cert_der)`
- Reconcile: §3 bullet is wrong. The actual formula is `sha256_hex(cert_der)`. Fix §3 OR add a note saying "see §4.1 for the load-bearing form."

### 3. `prevKeyId` placeholder

- **§1.3** mandates `""` at CBOR key 5 (so the canonical map always has 6 keys; the placeholder keeps the encoding deterministic when there's no previous key during normal operation)
- The JSON wire form (separate from the CBOR canonical signing input) may omit `prevKeyId` entirely when there's no rotation in flight
- Add a clarifying sentence to §1.3 distinguishing the two: "When `prevKeyId` is absent from the JSON wire form, the CBOR canonical-signing input MUST still include the key (CBOR map key 5) with an empty-string value. This keeps `bundleCanonical(bundle)` byte-identical regardless of whether the wire form serialized the field."

## What this does NOT require

- No test-vector changes (the vectors are correct; the docs are wrong).
- No code changes in cloister, the Python ref impl, or the spec wire docs other than the README.
- No bumping the spec version — these are clarifications, not semantic changes. The byte-level contract is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- `interlace-spec/0.1.0/README.md` reconciled on all three points.
- The Python ref impl conformance suite still passes (`python conformance/run.py` in `interlace-spec/0.1.0/ref-impl-py/`).
- A short "Errata" section at the top of the README documenting that 0.1.0 had these three doc inconsistencies, what the right answer is, and where each is fixed. So if a future implementor has an old README cached, they can still recover.

## Why a follow-up bead (not part of e61909)

The Python agent's brief was "make the spec falsifiable + flag ambiguities." It correctly did both — followed the vectors (the canonical answer), reported the doc bugs (the proper next step). Fixing the docs is its own ~30 min of work that doesn't need a fresh agent context.

## Refs

- `cloister-765132` — original spec extraction (closed). Spec was extracted from cloister's running code; doc/code inconsistencies survived translation.
- `cloister-e61909` — Python ref impl (closed). Surfaced the three issues + flagged that the test vectors were authoritative.
- `interlace-spec/0.1.0/ref-impl-py/conformance/run.py` — the regression suite that catches future doc drift.
title: Reconcile three Interlace spec README doc inconsistencies (claims-order, cert_fp definition, prevKeyId placeholder)

description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from a cross-repo coordination finding: the rosary image-ship agent (`rosary-16df06`) flagged that cloister's `udsForward` backend at `src/manifest/backends/uds-forward.ts:52` is a **stub that throws "not yet implemented"** when invoked. cluster.capnp's `transport = (uds = void)` declarations and the schema-reserved `Bundle.kind` for UDS-spoken siblings are all in tree — but the runtime path doesn't actually work. **Shipping that contradiction is incoherent.**

This bead is the "make the stub real" piece. The wire shape, codec, and schema are all already in tree — only the manifest-side dispatch is missing.

## What's already done (verified)

- **Wire schema** — `wire/cloister.capnp` + `wire/cross-check-fixtures.capnp` (per ADR-0005)
- **TS codec** — `src/wire/tool-call.ts` (encoder) + `src/wire/tool-result.ts` (decoder); cross-check'd against capnp CLI in `task wire:verify-roundtrip`
- **ADR-0005 amendment (2026-04-30)** — "cloister ↔ sibling bundles is plain capnp IPC inside the trust boundary, no AEAD"
- **Stub backend class** — `src/manifest/backends/uds-forward.ts` declares the `UdsForwardToolBackend` class with `tools()`, `handles()`, and a throwing `invoke()`
- **Cluster topology declarations** — `cluster.capnp` already wires mache + rosary as UDS siblings; `cluster:emit` generates compose entries with shared UDS volumes

## What's missing (this bead)

Replace the throwing `invoke()` with a real implementation that:

1. Connects to the sibling bundle's UDS socket (path comes from `spec.socketPath`, configured per-backend in the manifest).
2. Encodes the call via `src/wire/tool-call.ts` (canonical capnp `ToolCall` message).
3. Sends the encoded bytes over the UDS stream. **Workerd-on-CF doesn't support raw UDS connect from Worker code** — see "Substrate constraint" below.
4. Reads the response bytes from the UDS stream.
5. Decodes via `src/wire/tool-result.ts`.
6. Returns the result to the MCP layer.

## Substrate constraint (READ BEFORE STARTING)

**Cloudflare Workers / workerd Workers don't have raw socket APIs.** The Worker can't `connect("/run/cloister-uds/X.sock")` directly. ADR-0005 + cluster-be0607 anticipated this: the **cloister-companion** sidecar (`task companion:stub`) is the IPC seam.

Two design options:

### Option A — UDS via cloister-companion (preferred, matches ADR-0005 design)

The Worker calls cloister-companion over HTTP-on-loopback (workerd CAN do that), companion does the actual UDS connect to the sibling bundle, returns the response. The `socketPath` field on the backend spec is interpreted by companion, not the Worker.

This is what `LeylineNetToolBackend` already does for external network — `udsForward` becomes the in-pod analog using the same companion seam, just pointed at a UDS instead of TCP.

Required:
- Add a `udsForward` route handler in `cloister-companion` (the Rust sidecar at `companion/` or wherever). Wire it to the same capnp codec.
- `udsForward.invoke()` in cloister calls `companion.forward({transport: "uds", socketPath, body})`.
- `cluster.compose.yaml` mounts the shared UDS volume into BOTH cloister-router's container AND companion's container, so companion can `connect()` to it.

### Option B — UDS via Cloudflare TCP-shim binding

Cloudflare announced `connect()` for Workers in 2024. If workerd supports a UDS variant, the Worker could connect directly. Verify via workerd docs; if it works, the implementation is simpler (no companion in the path). Likely doesn't work for UDS today.

**Recommend Option A** — it's the ADR-0005 design, companion already exists, and it matches the LeylineNet pattern for external network. Option B is a follow-up if/when workerd gains UDS connect.

## Acceptance

- `UdsForwardToolBackend.invoke()` no longer throws "not implemented" — it routes a real call.
- New test at `test/manifest/uds-forward-backend.test.ts` exercises the full path against a stub UDS responder (or against `companion-stub` if Option A).
- `task cluster:up` with the default cluster.compose.yaml topology — rosary's image (per `rosary-16df06`) speaking capnp-over-UDS — gets reached from cloister-router's `tools/call` dispatch. Integration smoke test.
- `task lint` count grows by however many new tests; gate stays green.
- ADR-0005 amendment noting "udsForward backend landed via cloister-companion proxy" (or the alternative if you go Option B).

## Cross-repo coordination

If Option A: requires changes to **cloister-companion** (separate repo or directory — verify location). File a sibling bead there for the companion-side udsForward handler.

## Out of scope

- The actual UDS handshake protocol details beyond ToolCall/Result. capnp codec is already shipped.
- Multi-replica scaling (one companion per cluster).
- Per-bundle authn beyond the trust boundary (ADR-0005 says no AEAD inside the boundary; service-binding-as-capability is the gate).

## Refs

- `src/manifest/backends/uds-forward.ts:52` — the stub this bead retires
- `src/wire/tool-call.ts`, `src/wire/tool-result.ts` — codec already in tree
- `cluster.capnp` — declares the UDS wire across siblings
- `manifest/cluster.capnp` — schema reserving `Bundle.kind` for UDS-spoken bundles
- ADR-0005 (2026-04-30 amendment) — wire contract
- `cloister-be0607` — cluster topology this enables
- `rosary-16df06` — the cross-repo finding that surfaced this gap
title: Implement udsForward backend — make the stub real (capnp ToolCall/Result over UDS)

comments.text:
**2026-05-10 scope clarification**: dropping the "minimum-correct" option from the bead spec. User feedback was explicit: *"I DO NOT WANT MINIMUM CORRECT? that is tech debt."*

Right call. Half of the ADR-0012 handoff leaves you with:
- production attestation rows landing, BUT
- without content-addressed digests (so the disclosure endpoint can't link an attestation row to the canonical bytes a verifier would reconstruct), AND
- without the retry-queue path on the step-3 failure case (so a transient TrustStore RPC error silently drops the attestation; §13.2 false-positive when a peer audits later)

That's the worst of both worlds: a published security claim that's *partially* honored, where the partial honoring is invisible from the wire so neither operators nor peers can tell which case they're in.

**Updated scope = full ADR-0012 handoff:**

1. Compute canonical bead bytes (`src/storage/bead-canonical.ts`, already in tree)
2. `BlobStore.put(bytes) → digest` (idempotent, content-addressed; existing RPC)
3. `BeadStore.write({digest, bead_metadata})` — params now include the content digest
4. `TrustStore.applyAttestation({peerFingerprint, contentHash: digest, contentType: "bead/v1", scope, cert, sig, prevSelfRef, prevPeerRef, nowMs})`
5. On step-4 failure: enqueue `pending_attestations` (per `cloister-c6d378`); `TrustStore.drainPendingRetries` (per `cloister-fff647`) handles recovery
6. Cert + sig + scope come from the verified lease envelope — pass-through via the existing lease-middleware verification context (Option A from the original bead — RequestContext-style)

The `cloister-3dd355` fault-injection tests already cover the full multi-hop sequence. Production code mirrors what the tests already exercise; the tests become structural integration tests rather than test-only scaffolding.

Acceptance bar stays: a `disclosure/peers/<actor_fp>` request after a `bead_create` MUST return both counter rows AND attestation rows with valid `content_hash` values that round-trip against the BlobStore — proving §13.2 is runtime-load-bearing.

Ready to dispatch when prioritized.

description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from a real finding by `cloister-3dd355`: the cross-DO `bead_create` orchestration that threat-model §13.4 + ADR-0007 + ADR-0012 all describe **doesn't actually run in production.**

## The gap

`src/beads.ts:create()` currently does ONE thing: an intra-DO `INSERT INTO beads (...) VALUES (...)`. That's it.

What §13.4 + ADR-0012 describe (and what fault-injection tests in `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts` simulate):

```
bead_create →
  1. BlobStore.put(canonical_bead_bytes) → digest          (content-addressed, idempotent)
  2. BeadStore.write({digest, bead_metadata})              (per-repo DO; ACID)
  3. TrustStore.applyAttestation({peer_fp, digest, ...})   (singleton DO; signs the state-boundary)
```

**Step 1 and step 3 don't happen.** Today, a bead landing in cloister produces no BlobStore entry and no peer_attestations row. The §13.2 "silence is evidence" invariant — which requires every state-boundary write to have an attestation — is **structurally unenforceable** for actual production traffic, because there are no state-boundary writes being recorded.

The test orchestrator in `cloister-3dd355` IS doing all three steps, but only because the test harness wires them up. Production wires them up to BeadStore alone.

## Why this matters

The threat-model §8 "dangerous case" + ADR-0012's content-addressed handoff are **load-bearing for the substrate's security claim**. ADR-0007:154's original "same SQL transaction" rule was loosened to "ADR-0012 content-addressed handoff" — but neither rule binds anything if the orchestrator isn't actually doing the multi-step write.

Right now:
- `bead_create` succeeds without a content-addressed digest
- No peer_attestations row gets written
- A peer auditing `disclosure/peers/<actor_fp>` will see counter advances (from lease verify) but no attestation rows — exactly the §13.2 "silence" pattern that's supposed to indicate misbehavior
- A real third-party verifier would conclude cloister IS misbehaving — when actually, the substrate just hasn't wired the writes through yet

## What ships

1. **Move the bead_create dispatch** out of `src/beads.ts:create()` (the BeadStore DO method) and into a higher layer — likely `src/manifest/backends/durable-object.ts` or a new orchestrator at `src/routes/bead-create-orchestrator.ts`.

2. **Wire the three steps**:
   - Compute canonical bead bytes via `src/storage/bead-canonical.ts` (already exists; tested).
   - `BlobStore.put(bytes)` returns the digest. Idempotent.
   - `BeadStore.dispatch({method: "bead_create", params: {..., digest}})` — same RPC the manifest dispatches today, BUT the params now include the digest the BeadStore stores alongside the bead row.
   - `TrustStore.applyAttestation({peerFingerprint, contentHash: digest, contentType: "bead/v1", scope, cert, sig, prevSelfRef, prevPeerRef, nowMs})` — the attestation row that pins the state-boundary write.

3. **Recovery on failure**:
   - Step 1 fails: return error; no downstream writes. (BlobStore put is idempotent, so retry is safe.)
   - Step 2 fails: BlobStore digest already exists (idempotent), no bead row, no attestation. Retry rebuilds from canonical bytes → same digest → step 1 idempotent.
   - Step 3 fails: BlobStore + BeadStore landed; no attestation. Enqueue `pending_attestations` (per `cloister-c6d378` retry queue). Drain via `TrustStore.drainPendingRetries` (per `cloister-fff647`). This is the only step where production needs the queue.

4. **The fault-injection tests in `cloister-3dd355`** become structural integration tests instead of pure-test-only scaffolding. The test orchestrator that the agent wrote in the test file becomes the production orchestrator's MIRROR — both should call the same hops in the same order.

5. **Threat-model §13.4 + §8 honesty update**: replace any "tested" language with the actual disposition: "Cross-DO orchestration tested at `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts`; production orchestration shipped at `<path>` per this bead."

## Cert + scope inputs for step 3

The `applyAttestation` call needs cert + sig from the lease envelope. Today the lease middleware (`src/routes/lease-middleware.ts`) verifies and discards. The orchestrator needs the verified cert + sig + scope passed through. Two options:

- **A**: lease middleware writes the verified envelope into the request context (e.g. a `RequestContext` attached to `request.cf.cloisterLease`). The dispatcher reads it.
- **B**: pass cert + sig as explicit args from the lease middleware to the orchestrator.

Recommend A — it's the existing pattern for verified-state pass-through and doesn't require widening every backend's signature.

## What this is NOT

- NOT a re-do of `cloister-ee51b8` (which atomicized the SAME-DO `seen_nonces + lease_counter` writes). This is the OTHER cross-DO sequence (the state-boundary attestation, not the lease-counter advance).
- NOT a schema change. The DO method signatures are already there; the orchestrator just calls them in the right order with the right inputs.
- NOT speculative — the substrate's published security claim depends on this landing.

## Acceptance

- Production code path: every `tools/call bead_create` after lease verify performs all three hops.
- `test/security/cross-do-recovery.test.ts` (the existing fault-injection tests) passes against the production orchestrator, not just the test scaffolding.
- A `disclosure/peers/<actor_fp>` request after several bead_create calls returns BOTH counter rows AND attestation rows — proving the §13.2 invariant is actually live, not aspirational.
- Threat-model + §8 disposition flipped from "tested in fault-injection scaffolding" to "load-bearing in production code."
- `task lint` stays green; gate count grows by however many new integration tests.

## Refs

- §13.4 in `docs/security/threat-model.md` — the audit that surfaced the gap
- §8 (the dangerous case) — the failure mode this orchestrator's recovery path mitigates
- ADR-0007 — original transactional rule
- ADR-0012 — content-addressed handoff that replaces ADR-0007:154
- `cloister-3dd355` — fault-injection scaffolding that proves the shape is correct; closing this bead retires the "test-only orchestrator" framing
- `cloister-fff647` — `TrustStore.drainPendingRetries` for step-3 recovery
- `cloister-c6d378` — `pending_attestations` retry queue
- `cloister-ee51b8` — sibling-but-distinct: atomicized lease-counter writes inside TrustStore
title: Implement the real cross-DO bead_create orchestrator (BlobStore.put → BeadStore.write → TrustStore.applyAttestation)

description:
## Symptom

`cloister/rs/crates/sign/src/` is a hard fork of `ley-line-open/rs/ll-open/sign/src/` (the canonical leyline-sign per the lift commit `ley-line/3d805a6`, 2026-05-09). ll uses a symlink and stays in sync; cloister has diverged.

## Concrete diff (2026-06-24, post-LLO-v0.5.0)

Files only in cloister:
- `src/bin/` (the `leyline-sign-helper` binary, ADR-0019)
- `src/host/` (axum/hyper server + keyring client under `feature = "host"`)
- `src/cert_chain.rs`

Files in BOTH but diverged from LLO canonical:
- `src/cert.rs`, `src/cms.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/ffi.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/oid.rs`

## Why it happened

ADR-0019 (Accepted 2026-05-12) said "extend cloister/rs/crates/sign/ with a `[[bin]]` entry for the helper". But the leyline-sign lift to LLO was 2026-05-09 — three days BEFORE the ADR was accepted. The ADR didn't account for the new canonical home. Cloister has been drifting from LLO ever since.

A prior bead `cloister-bd8c41` (closed 2026-05-10) tracked the initial sync to ll-open 0.2.0. The sync was either incomplete at the time or re-diverged with subsequent host-side work.

## Proposed fix

Two options, picking one:

**(A)** Lift cloister's host extras (`bin/`, `host/`, `cert_chain.rs`) INTO LLO under `[features] host = []`, wasm-gated so workerd builds stay byte-identical. Then cloister symlinks to LLO (matching ll's pattern). One canonical crate, three consumer configs (wasm-verifier, host-helper, both). Linked ll-open bead.

**(B)** Cloister keeps a SEPARATE `cloister-sign-host` crate that depends on `leyline-sign` from LLO (path dep → eventually published crate). cloister/rs/crates/sign/ symlinks to LLO and stays verifier-only.

(A) is cleaner if LLO accepts the AGPL-3.0+ host code; (B) is cleaner if LLO wants to keep its license boundary unambiguous (LLO is mixed; cloister is AGPL-3.0+).

## Acceptance criteria

- cloister/rs/crates/sign/src is no longer a fork of LLO canonical
- Either symlink (A) or dep relationship (B) is in place
- ADR-0019 amended with the chosen fix
- `leyline-sign.wasm` artifact stays byte-identical pre/post fix (per ADR-0019's `cloister-2a0faa` invariant)

## Related

- Prior: `cloister-bd8c41` (closed; initial ll-open 0.2.0 sync)
- ADR-0019 (sign-only helper protocol) — needs amendment
- LLO canonical: `rs/ll-open/sign/Cargo.toml` v0.5.0
- Companion LLO bead: evaluate `[features] host` (option A enabling)
title: leyline-sign in cloister has drifted from LLO canonical since v0.5.0
